So four slots cannot all be plausible frontier improvements; the portfolio is one leader challenger, one leader-adjacent refinement, and one matched interaction pair on a revived background, balanced by two arms that preserve the known useful regime. remaining_sampling_rounds=0, so this allocation and the ranking are archive-only suggestions; no unexecuted array is claimed as a win and the cached leader needs no slot.
data.failure_directions: Named failure assumptions. (1) G2:H1 [8,5,5,0] assumes the 1→0 release slope continues through the near-zero guidance regime; a late-regime change would make it null or adverse and would fix interval3=1 as the usable endpoint. (2) G3:H2 [8,7,5,0] and G3:H1 [8,7,5,1] share one unverified extension — interval0=8 stacked with interval1=7 — so the two slots are not independent protection against that joint assumption failing; the measured +0.000392 adverse residual at interval3=3 is the specific rival. (3) G1:H1 [8,5,5,2] assumes the release gain is smooth at one tick; if release saturates at 3 it returns parity at best. (4) Duplicate IDs G2:H2/G3:H1/G4:H1 and G3:H2/G4:H2 are one experiment each under fixed R0 and a common random stream; a second copy is not independent evidence. (5) Delivery magnitude, matching instability or native relaxation may mediate every measured micro-effect, so none of these gaps identifies a mechanism. Gaps the supplied set cannot fill: no array varies interval2 or pairs interval1=6 with interval3=1, and none re-tests the cached leader; those gaps are disclosed rather than filled with invented arrays, and no unexecuted stack is claimed to win.
